notes: This skill ships no code, so there is no unit suite. Each fixture is a plain directory, not a git clone, because the skill must work without git. Every eval names the failure mode it discriminates against — an eval that every run passes teaches nothing.

evals.name: release-boundary-is-a-version
evals.expected_output: Names the next release as a version bump from 1.4.0, proposes a MoSCoW letter for all eight items, and reports that the Musts exceed roughly 60% of the 49-hour total if they do.
evals.failure_mode: Scoping to a calendar window ('the next two weeks') instead of a release. The package.json declares 1.4.0; a run that never mentions a version has ignored the one signal that makes MoSCoW meaningful here.
expectations: Reads package.json and names the release as a bump from 1.4.0
Assigns a letter to all eight items, none left blank
Gives a reason on every item whose proposed letter differs from its standing marker
Notices that rate-limit the login endpoint depends on session expiry and orders them accordingly
Computes the guard against the in-release total — Must plus Should plus Could, excluding Won't rows — and names the rows it summed, rather than asserting a figure without arithmetic
evals.result: pass, re-run against the corrected text — named the boundary as a bump from 1.4.0 and stated the assumed bump size rather than picking silently, lettered all eight items, caught the stated dependency, and computed the guard against the in-release total of 14 hr (Must+Should+Could), naming the rows summed. The earlier run of this eval reported a 49-hr denominator under a rule since replaced. This run also found the skill's worked examples reused this fixture's item names; the examples were renamed so a pattern-matching run cannot appear to pass.

evals.name: soft-cutoff-is-declared
evals.expected_output: States that the repo carries no version, that 'the next release' therefore means the next block of work, and that the cut-off is soft.
evals.failure_mode: Silently proceeding as though a hard release boundary exists, which overstates how much discipline the round carries. Inventing a version number is the same failure in a louder form.
expectations: Says explicitly that no version was found
Declares the cut-off soft rather than implying a firm boundary
Still completes the round — a soft boundary is a caveat, not a refusal
evals.result: pass, re-run against the corrected text — found no manifest, declared the boundary as the next block of work and said the cut-off is soft, and completed the round. The guard tripped at ~86% on the in-release denominator (1.5 of 1.75 hr) and was carried into Step 2 rather than blocking at Step 1.

evals.name: refuses-two-backlogs
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write, naming both docs/NEXT_STEPS.md and ROADMAP.md.
evals.failure_mode: Picking docs/NEXT_STEPS.md because it is first in the search order and writing to it. That silently ratifies a second backlog, the exact condition project-standard check 26 exists to prevent.
expectations: Refuses to write to either file
Does not triage the items anyway and offer to write later — the refusal comes before the round, not after
evals.result: pass — stopped at Step 0, named both files, ran no triage, and diff -r against the fixture was empty. The run exposed that the search order read as first-match-wins, which would have made this refusal unreachable; fixed in 43d9079 and re-run confirmed the amended wording leaves no room to guess.

evals.name: declines-the-uncomputable-guard
evals.expected_output: Runs the round and states that the 60% guard cannot be checked because no item carries an effort estimate.
evals.failure_mode: Producing a percentage anyway from invented effort figures. A fabricated number here is worse than no number, because it looks like the guard ran.
expectations: Assigns a letter to all five items
States that no effort estimates are present
Produces no percentage and no invented hour figures
evals.result: pass, re-run against the corrected text — lettered all five items, declined the guard explicitly, and stated no percentage, ratio or hour figure anywhere. Applied a Won't flavour using the spare-capacity test.

evals.name: separates-human-tasks-from-buildable
evals.expected_output: Letters only the three buildable rows. Moves the off-site backup purchase, the key rotation and the search-vendor decision to a Yours section, with what each needs. Treats the paid-ranking-tier row as a mixed row: scoped, but blocked by you.
evals.failure_mode: Assigning MoSCoW letters to work the assistant cannot perform. The key rotation is the sharpest case — the row says the CLI is user-only and blocked for automation, so a run that scopes it as a Must has scoped work it is structurally forbidden from doing.
expectations: Letters exactly three rows: thumbnailing, request logging, and the paid ranking tier
Moves the backup purchase, the key rotation and the vendor decision to a Yours section, none of them lettered
Gives no priority marker to any row under Yours
Treats the paid ranking tier as one row, scoped and marked blocked by you, rather than splitting or exiling it
Notes that the only near-term row in the file is not buildable, so the development scope has no urgent item
